chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Mu'ādhi, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Hamid, from Muhammad ibn Hafs, from Hafs ibn Ghiyath, from Layth, from Abd al-Malik, from Abi Bashir, from Hafsah bint Sirin, from Umm Sulayman, from the mother of Anas ibn Malik, that the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said:

When a woman dies and they wish to wash her, they should begin with her abdomen, and let it be wiped gently if she is not pregnant. But if she is pregnant, then do not move her. Then when you want to give her ghusl, begin with her lower part, and place a cloth over her private area. Then take a piece of cotton and wash her, and do well in washing her. Then insert your hand from beneath the cloth and wipe her with cotton three times, and do well in wiping her before you perform wudu for her. Then perform wudu for her with water in which lote leaves are mixed.
And he mentioned the rest of the hadith.

key_terms.تُوُفِّيَتِ: she passed away; referring to the death of the woman
key_terms.سِدْرٌ: lote leaves mixed in water for washing
key_terms.عَوْرَتِهَا: her private area that must be covered
key_terms.غُسْلَهَا: her ghusl (ritual washing of the deceased)
key_terms.كُرْسُفَةً: a piece of cotton used in cleansing
key_terms.يَغْسِلُوهَا: to wash her ritually after death

ai.seo_question: How should the body of a deceased woman be prepared and washed in Islamic law?
ai.summary: This hadith describes part of the procedure for the ghusl of a deceased woman, including gentleness, preserving modesty, and specific steps before wudu and washing. It reflects juridical guidance concerning ritual treatment of the deceased, especially in the case of pregnancy.
